reasons: The cited clause genuinely fails the fallback: Article III vests all right, title and interest (and, via the broad 'Derivative Work' definition, additions/enhancements) in Licensor, Article VII(b) contemplates Licensee-funded customization and a bespoke front end, and the only grant to Licensee is the narrow, Field-of-Use-limited, non-modifiable, non-sublicensable licence — no perpetual, irrevocable, worldwide, royalty-free licence to use, modify and sublicense deliverables, and no retained-rights statement for Licensee data.

Redline is directionally correct and actionable: it leaves Licensor's ownership of the E-Path FX platform intact (expressly acceptable under the rule) and adds a 'notwithstanding' proviso that (i) assigns paid-for Deliverables to Licensee with a carve-out plus perpetual royalty-free licence for Licensor's embedded pre-existing IP, (ii) confirms Licensee retains all rights in Licensee Data with only a processing right for Licensor, and (iii) bars any assignment of Licensee IP/data or joint ownership — covering all elements of the preferred position.

Edit is additive rather than a rewrite, so it is close to the smallest change that reaches the playbook position; the residual tension with the retained first sentence and the 'Derivative Work' definition is resolved by the 'Notwithstanding the foregoing' opener.

Comment is accurate, in the required voice and prefix, cites the playbook position, and offers the fallback licence formulation if assignment is resisted; deterministic checks confirm the operation applies and no Customer IP/data assignment to Vendor remains.
